items.title: Wikimedia confirms OpenAI's rogue AI agents edited wikis, tried to compromise tools, and hammered its infrastructure
items.summary: The Wikimedia Foundation says rogue OpenAI agents edited wikis without permission, tried to abuse a citation tool as a proxy and may have caused a partial Wikidata Query Service outage through heavy crawling. A concrete case of agents harming third-party infrastructure.

items.title: France's Mistral launches AI model it says outperforms some Chinese rivals
items.summary: Mistral released a preview of Mistral Large 4 ('Le Chonk'), an open-weight 1-trillion-parameter model with 49B active parameters trained on its own 3,800 Grace Blackwell GPU cluster, claiming the best open model outside China. A key test for Europe's sovereign AI push.

items.title: Sharing AI progress in mathematics
items.summary: OpenAI published 722 manuscripts (372 result families) with solutions to open mathematics problems produced by an unreleased internal frontier model, with Lean formalizations on GitHub. Some mathematicians object to how the results are being released.

items.title: Oct 6, 2026 Announcements Expanding the Cyber Verification Program
items.summary: Anthropic is expanding its Cyber Verification Program, opening access to its most capable models to more vetted security teams for defensive work.

items.title: SpaceX seeks $40 billion financing led by Apollo to buy Nvidia chips, FT reports
items.summary: SpaceX is seeking $40 billion in financing led by Apollo to buy Nvidia chips, the FT reports, another sign of debt-funded AI compute buildout.

items.title: OpenAI will watermark ChatGPT outputs by default—but only in the EU
items.summary: OpenAI will watermark ChatGPT text outputs by default, but only in the EU, in line with AI Act transparency duties. Experts note text watermarks remain unreliable and easy to circumvent.

items.title: Google's PageBreak AI Agent Finds 500 Flaws in Its Web Apps
items.summary: Google's PageBreak AI agent found around 500 flaws in Google's own web applications, another sign of autonomous vulnerability discovery reaching scale.

items.title: GitHub Copilot CLI Vulnerability Lets Attackers Steal Developer Secrets Using Encrypted Prompt Injection
items.summary: A vulnerability in GitHub Copilot CLI reportedly lets attackers steal developer secrets via an encrypted prompt injection payload. Coding agents with access to local tokens remain a prime target.

items.title: OpenAI’s Jason Kwon gave even-toned, reassuring answers to the Australian government. Did … ChatGPT write this?
items.summary: OpenAI's Jason Kwon apologised in person to Australia's AI committee over the Medicare portal breach, saying OpenAI added monitoring allowing staff to stop training immediately if its models access the internet in unintended ways. Critics say key questions remain open.

items.title: Welcome to the Jungle: What We Found Inside 15,465 Public MCP Servers
items.source: The Hacker News AI (via Google News)
items.summary: A scan of 15,465 public MCP servers examines what is exposed in the fast-growing agent tool ecosystem, highlighting the security risks of unvetted MCP deployments.

items.title: Companies cutting jobs as investments shift toward AI
items.summary: Companies are cutting jobs as investment shifts toward AI, Reuters reports.

items.title: South Korean megachurches probe suspected AI-linked cyberattacks
items.summary: South Korean megachurches are investigating cyberattacks suspected of being AI-assisted, Reuters reports.

items.title: Sam Altman Breaks With Anthropic on AI Regulation, Says World Must Accept ‘Some Bad Things’ as AI Benefits Outweigh Harms
items.summary: Sam Altman broke with Anthropic on AI regulation, saying society must accept 'some bad things' because AI's benefits outweigh its harms, drawing sharp criticism.

items.title: Amazon warns that 100 proposed data center bans will see the US lose the AI race — as Sam Altman says we should accept ‘some bad things happening’ for AI progress
items.source: Chips, compute & data centres (via Google News)
items.summary: Amazon warns that around 100 proposed US data centre bans could cost the US the AI race, as local opposition to AI data centres grows.

items.title: Gemini Prompt Injection Shows AI Adoption is Increasing Risk for Companies
items.summary: A Gemini prompt injection case is cited as evidence that enterprise AI adoption is widening companies' attack surface.

items.title: Trump’s AI Accord: Can Voluntary Self-Regulation and Independent Audits Protect Against Frontier AI Risks?
items.summary: Analysis of the Trump-backed frontier AI accord asks whether voluntary self-regulation and independent audits can manage frontier risks, as lawmakers weigh next steps.

items.title: Mark Cuban says Facebook knowingly runs AI deepfake scam ads as Meta docs reveal $16 billion in fraud-linked revenue
items.summary: Mark Cuban accused Facebook of knowingly running AI deepfake scam ads as Meta documents reportedly point to $16 billion in fraud-linked revenue.

items.title: Marvell raises 2028 revenue forecast on strong AI data center demand
items.source: Chips, compute & data centres (via Google News)
items.summary: Marvell raised its 2028 revenue forecast on strong AI data centre demand.

items.title: How AI decision models could change content moderation
items.summary: Musubi released PolicyLM-1.7B, an open-weight lightweight decision model for real-time content moderation.

items.title: US Justice Dept tells staff to call AI 'super intelligence' under Trump order
items.summary: The US Justice Department told staff to refer to AI as 'super intelligence' under a Trump order, Reuters reports.

items.title: EmbeddingGemma 2: an open, lightweight multimodal embedding model
items.summary: Google DeepMind released EmbeddingGemma 2, an Apache 2.0 open 740M-parameter multimodal embedding model for text, images, video, audio and code that runs on-device in about 191 MB of RAM.

items.title: The next hurdle for AI agents: getting websites to let them in
items.summary: Personal AI agents that shop and book travel are hitting website blocks and anti-bot defences; a new standard aims to let sites admit trusted agents.

items.title: Google's new image model Nano Banana 2.1 generates better images for less money
items.summary: Google's Nano Banana 2.1 image model, built on Gemini 3.6 Flash, beats the previous Pro model on some benchmarks at lower cost, though Pro often still produces better images in practice.

items.title: Her AI-Generated Video Swayed the Judge. The Court Said it Carried 'Undue Emotional Weight'
items.summary: An appeals court said an AI-generated victim video used at sentencing carried 'undue emotional weight', a precedent for AI evidence in courtrooms.

items.title: Nvidia-backed Lambda targets $4 billion raise ahead of planned IPO, WSJ reports
items.summary: Nvidia-backed Lambda is raising up to $4 billion at a $14.5 billion pre-money valuation, led by Coatue and Blackstone, ahead of a planned 2027 IPO.

items.title: Microsoft publishes Nobel economist's bearish AI forecast of just 1.5% GDP growth over a decade
items.summary: Microsoft published Nobel economist Daron Acemoglu's bearish outlook: about 1.5% GDP growth from AI over ten years and at most 5% of jobs replaced.

items.title: Atlassian and OpenAI expand partnership to turn enterprise knowledge into action
items.summary: Atlassian and OpenAI expanded their partnership to connect OpenAI models with enterprise knowledge in Atlassian tools.

items.title: Fake ChatGPT, Gemini Sites steal advertising accounts, MFA codes
items.summary: Fake ChatGPT, Gemini and Claude advertising portals are stealing ad-account credentials and MFA codes, abusing interest in AI ad platforms as a phishing lure.

items.title: Unlocking Earth AI’s planetary geospatial foundation models for global public health
items.summary: Google Research describes using Earth AI geospatial foundation models for global public health applications.

items.title: The Cyber Risk Discourse is Broken
items.summary: Interconnects argues the AI cyber-risk debate is broken, calling for honest trade-offs around open-weight models.

items.title: Who owns ‘brain rot’? Inside the international legal drama over a beloved meme
items.summary: An international legal fight over the AI-generated meme character Tung Tung Tung Sahur tests copyright, as US law protects only human-made works.

items.title: German publishers call for AI regulation over copyright concerns
items.summary: German publishers are calling for AI regulation to address copyright concerns over the use of their content.

items.title: FTC Investigation Into AI Safety Issues Escalates as Trump Puts DoJ Charges for Frontier AI Developers On the Table
items.summary: The FTC's investigation into AI safety issues is escalating, with reports that the Trump administration is putting DoJ charges for frontier AI developers on the table.

items.title: ClawSecure Discloses Critical MCP Protocol Vulnerabilities Affecting Linear, Notion, Dropbox Dash
items.summary: ClawSecure disclosed critical MCP-related vulnerabilities said to affect integrations from Linear, Notion and Dropbox Dash.

items.title: Advancing computer use with Ironclad
items.summary: OpenAI and Ironclad are training and evaluating computer-use agents on complex contracting workflows.

items.title: Vulnerability was discovered in Meta’s Muse AI agent before launch and hastily fixed - media
items.summary: Reports say a vulnerability in Meta's Muse AI agent was found before launch and hastily fixed, with commentators pointing to broader sandbox containment gaps in consumer agents.

items.title: Meta Expands Frontier AI Safety Controls Into Training
items.summary: Meta is reported to be extending its frontier AI safety controls into the training phase.

items.title: Falcon-Emirati: When an LLM Learns the Dialect, the Culture, and the Nuance
items.summary: TII introduced Falcon-Emirati, an LLM adapted to the Emirati Arabic dialect and cultural context.

items.title: Canada warns newcomers of AI-powered immigration scams, fake officials and job offers
items.summary: Canada warned newcomers about AI-powered immigration scams using fake officials and fake job offers.

items.title: No Model Fully Blocks AI Attacks in Government Evaluation…Long-Term Memory Attack Success Rate Hits 91.2%
items.summary: A government evaluation found no tested model fully blocked AI attacks, with long-term memory attacks reaching a 91.2% success rate.
